newsitem.title: UK: Four ships boycotted in European action - ITF.
newsitem.headline: Four ships boycotted in European action - ITF.

text.p: Ships in four countries were subjected to boycotts and delays on the second day of a week long European campaign against flags of convenience, the International Transport Workers' Federation (ITF) said Tuesday.
Transport trade unions held up ships in Portugal, Norway, Croatia and Sweden, the ITF claimed.
The ITF said Norwegian dockers at Narvik boycotted the Leon, a U.S.-owned 128,000 dwt bulk carrier, delaying the vessel.
The Panamanian-registered 29,400 dwt bulk carrier Sharpnes was held up in Leixoes, Portugal while an ITF agreement was negotiated for its Russian crew, the union added.
The ITF also said a small German bulker was held up in the Croatian port of Rijeka and a Cypriot-flag general cargo ship was boycotted in Gothenburg, Sweden.

The term flag of convenience refers to ships flying the flag which is not the national flag of the country of the owner. The ITF has long said FOC registers tend to have more substandard ships and poorer wages than national registers.
